articles.title: Psychiatrists detail mother’s sudden descent into severe psychosis and delirious mania following childbirth
articles.summary: A recent case report details a 27-year-old mother’s sudden onset of severe psychosis and delirious mania following a cesarean delivery. The findings suggest that electroconvulsive therapy can provide rapid relief for this life-threatening postpartum psychiatric emergency.

articles.title: Neuroticism intensifies the transfer of fear and negativity during associative learning
articles.summary: People who score high in neuroticism not only react more intensely to negative events, but they also transfer those bad feelings onto neutral objects more easily. New research highlights how personality traits shape our vulnerability to anxiety.

articles.title: A computational model explains the sudden rise in societal division
articles.summary: A new computational model reveals that simply increasing the number of close social connections past a certain threshold naturally forces society to splinter into deeply divided, polarized echo chambers.

articles.title: Regular coffee beats decaf in protecting the brain from chronic stress, mouse study finds
articles.summary: A new study in mice indicates that caffeinated coffee prevents stress-induced memory loss and depression-like behaviors, while decaf offers no such protection. The findings suggest caffeine is the key ingredient for coffee's mood-boosting benefits.

articles.title: A longer exhale may push your brain toward bolder decisions
articles.summary: Slow breathing with a prolonged exhale made people more willing to take risks by changing heart activity and increasing the brain’s sensitivity to rewards. The findings suggest that something as simple as controlling your breath can directly influence how you evaluate choices.

articles.title: Scientists reveal the hidden instructions that build the human brain
articles.summary: UCLA researchers have discovered two powerful influences that help guide how the human brain forms before birth. Radial glia, stem cells responsible for producing much of the cerebral cortex, change their behavior depending on how they process glucose and on physical contact with signals arriving from the thalamus. Those signals can alter which types of neurons are produced, including upper-layer neurons that are especially prominent in humans.

articles.title: Stanford scientists discover a seafood that can reverse signs of aging
articles.summary: A substance found in edible sea squirts appeared to reverse several signs of aging in older mice. Plasmalogen supplements improved memory and learning, strengthened connections between brain cells, reduced inflammation, and even helped the mice grow thicker, darker hair. Researchers believe the compounds may encourage brain regeneration and protect aging synapses.

articles.title: New injectable treatment helps the brain rebuild after stroke
articles.summary: Duke researchers developed an injectable scaffold that helped stroke-damaged brains grow new blood vessels, support nerve regrowth, and recover movement in mice. The treatment appears to work partly by recruiting the body’s own immune cells, including neutrophils that may switch from damaging to helpful under the right conditions.

articles.title: Structure and Implementation of New Practical English Textbooks Driven by Artificial Intelligence
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.02981v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence is changing the form of applied English materials from fixed paper sequences to adaptive learning systems that can diagnose learners, recommend tasks, and provide formative feedback. This paper studies the structure and application of a new practical English textbook driven by artificial intelligence. A five-layer architecture is proposed: knowledge mapping, learner profiling, task generation, feedback orchestration, and teacher-side governance. A prototype was tested on 186 non-English-major undergraduates for eight weeks

articles.title: Fresh Memory, Stale Plans: Dependency-Scoped Validation for Distributed LLM-Agent Memory
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.03340v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distributed LLM-agent teams can read the latest shared facts and still act on an obsolete plan. A planner may derive an action from requirement $r_3$, another agent may commit $r_4$, and an executor may receive $r_4$ without replacing the plan derived from $r_3$. We call this \emph{stale-plan execution}: state freshness does not establish that the plan authorizing an action remains valid. We introduce PlanFence, a dependency-scoped action-validation protocol. Plans cite the exact public records they used, and an executor validates only the record

articles.summary: arXiv:2609.02959v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: What does a language model predict when it has few clues? articles.summary: arXiv:2609.02986v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hybrid architectures combining Full Attention (FA) and Linear Attention (LA) are increasingly prominent, yet their allocation remains heuristic. We seek an evidence-grounded basis in head-level functional organization learned by RoPE-based Transformers.
